title: Partitions
subtitle: Sharding topics across brokers for horizontal write throughput and parallel consumer scaling.
keyTakeaways: The partition is the fundamental atomic unit of scalability and concurrency in Kafka: a topic is physically split into N independent partitions.
Kafka guarantees message ordering strictly *within a single partition*, never across an entire topic.
Records with the same message key are routed to the same partition using Murmur2 hashing (`murmur2(key) % num_partitions`), guaranteeing per-entity ordering.

(Each broker owns 1 Leader partition; writes scale horizontally across all 3 nodes!)

sections.heading: Physical Storage Sharding and Key Routing
sections.body: A single Kafka topic cannot scale beyond the disk and network limits of a single machine unless it is partitioned. A partition is an ordered, immutable sequence of messages stored on disk as a folder of segment files. Partitions are distributed across brokers in the cluster. When producing a message, Kafka determines the destination partition using its routing key.
bullets: Key-Based Hashing: If a message key is provided (e.g., `user_id = 98124`), the producer computes `murmur2(key) % num_partitions`. All events for that user land on the same partition in sequential order.

Round-Robin / Sticky Partitioning: If the message key is null, the producer uses Sticky Partitioning: batching messages together and sending them to a single partition until the batch fills or `linger.ms` expires, maximizing network compression before switching to the next partition.

sections.heading: Mitigating Hot Partitions and Key Skew
sections.body: While key hashing guarantees per-entity ordering, it exposes the cluster to partition skew. If 80% of your platform's transactions belong to a single enterprise customer or celebrity, hashing by `user_id` routes 80% of all writes to a single partition. That partition's broker suffers disk I/O and CPU saturation, while other partitions sit idle.
bullets: Compound Keys / Salting: Append a randomized suffix to high-volume hot keys (`celebrity_id#1`, `celebrity_id#2`) to scatter events across multiple partitions. Trade-off: consumers lose strict ordering across the salted sub-partitions.
Composite Entity Routing: Route by a finer-grained attribute (e.g., routing by `order_id` instead of `store_id`) so individual store transactions distribute evenly across all partitions.

tradeOffs.pros: Enables up to 64 concurrent consumer instances; higher aggregate read and write throughput.
tradeOffs.cons: Consumes more open file descriptors on brokers; increases failover recovery time during broker reboots.
tradeOffs.bestFor: High-throughput ingest topics processing 50,000+ events per second.

tradeOffs.pros: Minimal memory and file descriptor overhead; fast leader election failover.
tradeOffs.cons: Restricts consumer concurrency to at most 4 active consumers in a group.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Low-volume administrative events, configuration updates, and audit trails.

interviewTip: Never say Kafka guarantees total ordering across a topic. Clarify immediately: 'Kafka guarantees strict message ordering only within an individual partition. To guarantee causal ordering for a specific user or account, we must use that ID as the message key so all related events route to the same partition.'
